CABOT ANNOUNCES DECEMBER EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH

While each employee of the month announcement is special, this one in particular has extra importance.
Not only is this employee being recognized for his achievement over the last few months and beyond; but
for his part in helping turn an entire Department around. In addition to being named employee of the
month, this month’s winner will receive something extra.

Therefore, in front of the entire City, family, and co-workers, the City of Cabot recognizes Dwayne
Boswell as the employee of the month for December for his hard work and dedication during the month
of November and beyond. In addition, officially as of tonight, Dwayne will no longer be just the interim
Fire Chief, but the City is proud to announce him as the permanent Fire Chief.

Midway through the year, it was obvious that a major change was needed in the Fire Department.
Wanting to make the right decision and not rush to a new hire, Dwayne along with the other two Battalion
Chiefs, Louis Cimino and Jim Firebaugh, were put in charge while things were sorted out. All three of
these men took on a very difficult assignment and did an amazing job. This cannot be overstated.

As the search began for a Fire Chief, Chief Boswell stepped forward and expressed his desire to run the
Department. His vision was a Fire Department where guys felt like family again and were excited to come
to work each day. He wanted the Fire Department to be a team member of the City’s administration and
take an approach to leadership that benefits everyone. After a long search and speaking with candidates
from both locally and across the US, Chief Boswell was named the interim Chief on October 21*. In
almost two months to the day, the City is seeing the rewards of this decision.

Chief Boswell has opened things up to the Fire Department from the top to the bottom. Ideas and
suggestions are flowing and many changes have already been made. Simple things from filling shifts to
clothing options were instantaneous. In conjunction with Police, a charity kickball game was held. The
amount of off duty and on duty firefighters and their families present was impossible not to notice. As has
been publicized, the Fire Department recently raised $12,788 for their Cabot Christmas for Kids program.
Tonight’s meeting has a resolution for a quick response vehicle. Promotions were just done through
assessment centers and outside feedback. The list goes on and on. Just visiting each station and seeing the
difference of the interaction of the men and their demeanor is so difficult to put in words.

The decision to make Chief Boswell the permanent Chief was most evident though by the amount of
Firefighters who have approached the Mayor and Human Resources in the last two months. Each of them
not only shared their excitement for the new direction of the Department, but many of them kept asking
the same question: when would the interim tag be removed?

For being chosen employee of the month, he will receive a plaque with his name on it, his name added to
the list of employees chosen as employee of the month on the City Hall plaque, his story in the
newspaper, his photo and name added to the City website, and lunch or breakfast with the Mayor and the
Human Resources Director.

ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS AMENDING ORDINANCE
NO. 1-1963 TO CHANGE THE ANNUAL PAYMENT RECEIVED FROM
TELEPHONE COMPANY FOR USE OF PUBLIC RIGHTS OF WAYS

WHEREAS, on or about January 14, 1963 the City of Cabot, Arkansas (the “City”)
adopted Ordinance No. 1-1963 granting to Southwestern States Telephone Company the
right to use the public rights of ways to operate its Telephone System and all business
incidental to or connected with the conducting of a Telephone business in exchange for an
annual payment from the Company to the City; and

WHEREAS, CenturyTel of Arkansas, Inc. d/b/a CenturyLink (the “Company”)
acquired the Telephone System serving the City and is the successor in interest to
Southwestern States Telephone Company under Ordinance No. 1-1963; and

WHEREAS, Arkansas Code § 14-200-101 authorizes municipalities to require
telecommunications service providers to pay a franchise fee to operate within the local
government boundaries; and

WHEREAS, the City and Company have agreed to amend Ordinance No. 1-1963 to
change the annual payment made to the City.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, that the Mayor and Council of the City
of Cabot, Arkansas hereby amend Ordinance No. 1-1963 to change the quarterly payment
made to the City subject to the following conditions the Company and the City have
previously agreed:

SECTION 1: That, Section 7 of Ordinance No. 1-1963 is hereby amended to
increase the current payment from two percent (2%) of its gross revenues to four and one
quarter percent (4.25%) to be paid quarterly to City.

SECTION 2: This amendment of Ordinance No. 1-1963 and the provisions of said

Ordinance amended hereby shall be effective immediately upon passage.

SECTION 4.14 SIGNS
Amended by Ordinance 1 of 2020

4.14.1 Purpose and Intent

The purpose and intent of this section is to support and complement the various land uses allowed in the
City of Cabot (“City”) through appropriate, acceptable types of signs for business and event needs. The
Standards contained herein are intended to ensure consistency in style, scale, visibility, readability, and
clarity as well as location and quantity, while allowing for a varied, exciting, and interesting visual landscape.
More specifically, the purpose of this code is to:

Encourage the effective use of signs as a means of communication in the City.
Stay compliant with State and Federal statutes.

Protect the public welfare and City property values by preserving the aesthetic and
environmental qualities of the City.

Protect pedestrians and motorists of the City from damage or injury caused or partially attributed
to the distractions caused by improper size, location, or upkeep of signs.

Maintain the economic viability of businesses in our community through the availability of
appropriate signage.

To promote public safety, health, welfare, convenience, and enjoyment of travel and the free flow
of travel within the City.

4.14.2 Permit Review, Issuance, and Inspection

a.

Permit Required:

Unless specifically exempted in this code, no sign allowed by this code shall be constructed, erected,
moved, enlarged, illuminated, altered, or displayed without first being issued a sign permit when
applicable in accordance with the standards of this code. In addition to a sign permit, a Building Permit
may or may not be required. It is the responsibility of the business owner to verify with the City if a
Building Permit is required.

Application for Permit:

Applications for initial sign permits shall be made upon forms provided by the City and shall contain
or have attached thereto the following information:

i. Applicant name, address, telephone number and email address.
ii. Building owner’s name, address, telephone number and email address.

iii. Location of the building, structure, or lot which the sign or other advertising structure is to be
attached or erected.

iv. Position of the sign or other advertising structure in relation to nearby buildings or structures.

v. Two blueprints or drawings (digital or paper) of the plans and specifications, the method of
construction and attachment to the building or in the ground.

vi. Name of person, firm, corporation, or association erecting structure. EXHIBIT

viii. Any electrical permit required and issued for said sign. Application requesting electrical permit

Permit Fees:

i. Temporary sign fee - $10.00, per application

Review of Permit Application:

The Code Official or designee must promptly process the Sign permit application and approve the
application, reject the application, or notify the applicant of deficiencies in the application within ten (10)
business days after receipt. Any application that complies with all provisions of this Code, the zoning
ordinance, the building code, and other applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances shall be approved.

Rejection of Permit Application:

If the Sign permit application is rejected, the Code Official shall provide a list of the reasons for the
rejection in writing. An application must be rejected for non-compliance with the terms of this Code, the
zoning ordinance, building code, or other applicable law, regulation, or ordinance.

Issuance of Permit:

It shall be the duty of the Code Official or designee, upon the filing of an application for a sign permit, to
examine such plans, specifications and the premises upon which it is proposed to erect the sign or other
advertising structure. If the proposed structure and sign are in full compliance with all requirements of
this code, all other laws and codes of the City, the sign permit shall be issued within ten (10) days. If the
Code Official or designee fails or rejects a completed sign application because it fails to show full
compliance with all code requirements, he/she shall notify the applicant within ten (10) days as to why
such application fails to meet all code requirements.

. Permit Tolling Period:
If the work authorized under a sign permit has not been completed within six (6) months after date of

issuance, the said permit shall become null and void.

For temporary signs, unless authorized in other sections of this Code, if the work authorized under a
temporary sign permit has not been completed within thirty (30) days, the said permit shall become null
and void.

Inspection of Permit:

Any person installing, structurally altering, or relocating a sign for which a permit has been issued shall
notify the City upon completion. A final inspection will be required, including electrical inspection if
needed.

Responsibility for Compliance by Permittee:

All businesses or organizations interested in installing signs are responsible for acquiring such permits.
Signage may be selected from the allowable options indicated herein and design drawings must be
submitted for approval by the City prior to installation of said signage.

4.14.3 Permits Not Required

a. Authorized Signs. Other than signs specifically prohibited in this code, Authorized Signs with a total

b. Official Notices. Official notices or advertisements posted or displayed by or under the direction of any

must be removed no more than ten (10) days after their purpose has been accomplished

4.14.4 Variances

Fee — 250.00: Any final administrative decision rendered in denying a permit may be appealed to
the Board of Adjustments for a variance. A variance is not allowed for Prohibited Signs of this code.
The request for variances shall be in writing and shall be submitted along with the sign application.
Such request shall demonstrate that special conditions or circumstances exist that is not applicable
to other lands, structures, or buildings such that an interpretation of this code would result in an
undue hardship. Requests for variance made to the Board of Adjustments shall be in writing and
shall state the nature of the appeal. The Board of Adjustments shall review all requests to determine
if variance should be granted. If the Board of Adjustments denies the variance request, the applicant
may appeal to the Circuit Court.

4.14.5 Nonconforming Signs

For the purpose of this section, a nonconforming sign shall be defined as a sign which does not
conform to the provisions of this code. All nonconforming signs/structures not otherwise prohibited
by the provisions of this code, relating to a place of business and located on the same premises as
such place of business, may be continued unless:

a. The business is closed or abandoned for six (6) months and the sign/sign structure fails to meet
the requirements of the Maintenance section of this code.

b. The sign/sign structure is destroyed by any means to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%).

c. The owner may request permission of the Board of Adjustments to reconstruct the sign/sign
structure and continue the nonconforming use. The Board of Adjustments may grant or deny the
request. In granting the request to reconstruct, the Board of Adjustments may require conformance
to setbacks, electrical code, land and lighting requirements.

4.14.6 Allowable Signs

1. Signs are prohibited in all Zoning Districts unless:
a. Constructed pursuant to a valid building permit when required by this Code; and
b. Authorized under this Code.

2. Prohibition of Fees:
A property owner may not accept a fee for posting or maintaining a Sign allowed under Section
1.C.ii and any sign that is posted or maintained in violation of this provision is prohibited.

3. Commercial Signs in Residential Zones:
Commercial Signs are prohibited in exclusively single-family residential zones or on property used for
non-transient residential uses, except for those properties on which a home occupation or a
transient residential use has been approved by the City of Cabot.

4.14.12 Illumination
a. Neon:

i. Neon is allowed for wall signs or projecting signs only. Neon must be affixed to a sign backing.
ii. Lettering or logos directly hanging on the fascia of the building are prohibited.

iii. Neon may only be utilized for the name of the principle use, with minimal ancillary lettering or
logo incorporated into the sign face.

iv. One (1) Neon sign per building is allowed, and is limited to 0.5 sq. ft. per 1 linear foot ofwall
space. Any additional signage allowed (Wall Signs) must be non-illuminated.

v. Neon is prohibited for any use other than specific lettering or logo signage. Architectural neon
lighting (for example outlining windows) is prohibited.

b. Exterior Illumination:

i. If Illumination is external, it shall be located and directed solely at the sign.

ii. The light source shall not be visible from or cast into the right-of-way, or cause glare hazards to
pedestrians, motorists, or adjacent properties.

iii. The light source shall not be mounted to any part of the sign.

iv. Only one exterior light shall be permitted per sign face for signs 16 square feet or less, andtwo
exterior lights for sign faces that exceed 16 square feet in size.

c. Interior Illumination:

i. A Channel Illuminated Sign is a sign whose light source is located in the interior of a sign so that light
illumination shines through the front surface of the sign in specific “cut-away” areas. Any words,
lettering, figures, numerals, emblems, devices, trademarks, or trade names, or any combination
thereof, by which anything is made known and which is designed to attract attention and/or convey a
message, may be displayed by channel cutting the words, letters, figures, etc. out of the surface of the
sign. The sign itself is illuminated through cuts, or channels made through the surface of the sign.

ii. A push-thru acrylic sign is typically an internally illuminated sign with letters and/or logos cut out of
translucent acrylic that is as thick or thicker than the opaque sign face material, and mounted on the
inside of the sign face so that the acrylic material’s thickness extends flush with our pushing through
and beyond the front plane of the sign face. Acrylic letters are raised from the surface of the sign face
so that light passes through the edges. Acrylic that extends beyond the front plane may also have a
face of all letters/logos to create a back light effect if desired.

iii. A maximum of 10 foot candles is permitted on any portion of the sign. A foot candle is defined as a
unit of luminance or light falling onto a surface. It stands for the light level on a surface one foot from
a standard candle.

iv. All lighting shall meet all applicable electrical codes.

4.14.13 Alternative Signage Plans

An Alternative Signage Plan may be used where impractical situations would result from this code.
Alternative locations, size or quantity may be justified due to topography, utility easements, lot
configuration or subdivision (particularly with respect to a shopping center), or location and size of pre-
existing development. Also, the proposed use or collection of uses may not be captured by the spirit and
intent of this code, justifying an Alternative Signage Plan. The Planning Commission shall approve an
Alternative Signage Plan if it meets the purpose and intent of the sign code. The following conditions
shall be met in order for an Alternative Signage Plan to be considered for approval:

a. The applicant must show that installation of signage per this code while meeting other site-specific
constraints as listed above would put the site in direct violation of other City Ordinances or State or
Federal regulations, under any practical site layout configuration.

b. The use(s) and/or architectural elements proposed for the site (as already approved by the Planning
Department) are such that a standard sign plan under this code would be considered not in keeping
with the code.

4.14.14 Electronic Message Signs
a. Sign Type: Electronic message signs shall only be allowed on monument mounted and pole signs.

b. Size: The maximum sign area of the electronic portion of an electronic message sign shall not
exceed 50 square feet.

c. Dimming and Brightness: Signs shall be equipped with dimming technology that automatically adjusts
the display brightness based on ambient light conditions. The sign shall not exceed 0.3 foot candles
illumination above ambient light level.

d. Movement: The illusion of movement by means of a preprogrammed (repetitious or sequential)
switching action in which illuminated elements of the sign are turned off or on to visually simulate the
impression of motion characteristic of chasing, running, blinking, oscillating, twinkling, scintillating, or
expanding and contracting light patterns, is prohibited.

e. Rate of Change: No electronic message sign shall change copy more frequently than once during
any eight (8) second intervals. Electronic message signs that only display the time, temperature, or
both the time and the temperature, may change at real time.

f. Allowable Zones: As allowed by the MONUMENT SIGN & PYLON SIGN Section of this Code.

4.14.15 Maintenance

All sign(s)/sign structure and premises surrounding the same shall be maintained by the owner thereof in
aclean, sanitary condition and free and clear of all rubbish and weeds. All components thereof, including
supports, braces, anchors, etc., shall be kept in compliance with all building and electrical codes, and in
conformance with the requirements of this Code. All components should be free from deterioration, termite
infestation, rot, rust or loosening. Repair and replacement of any faded, peeled, cracked or otherwise
damaged or broken parts of a sign is required by this Code.

ORDINANCE NO. __ OF 2020
AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND VARIOUS SECTIONS OF THE CODE OF CABOT,
CHAPTER 4 ANIMALS FOR THE CITY OF CABOT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, it is the intent of the City Council of the City of Cabot, Arkansas to amend the
Code of Cabot and adopt the new Animal Control regulations set forth below in an effort to
encourage the humane treatment of animals.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:
SECTION 1: Chapter 4, Animals, Article I. – In General, § 4-1. – Definitions
is hereby amended to add and/or modify the following definitions:
Community Cat - Any free-roaming cat that may be cared for by one or more residents of
the immediate area who is/are known or unknown; a community cat may or may not be feral.
Working Cat means any free-roaming cat that may or may not be feral and "works" for its
upkeep by hunting vermin, such as rodents and is cared for by an individual or business
proprietor.
Eartipping – The removal of the 1⁄4-inch tip of a Community Cat’s left ear, performed
while the cat is under anesthesia. The purpose of eartipping is to identify the Community Cat as
being sterilized and lawfully vaccinated for rabies.
SECTION 2: Chapter 4, Animals, Article I. – In General § 4-1. – Definitions
is hereby amended to delete the following definitions:
Feral cat caretaker means any person or organization, other than an owner, who provides
food, water, shelter or otherwise cares for a feral cat.
Feral cat colony means a group of cats that congregate as a unit. Although not every cat in a
colony may be feral, any non-feral cats that congregate with a colony shall be deemed to be a
part of it.
Feral cat colony caretaker means any feral cat caretaker who is approved by city animal
services to care for a feral cat colony.

SECTION 3: Chapter 4, Animals, Article III. – Animal Care and Control § 4-61. –
Releasing Animals In Public Places in the Corporate City Limits is hereby amended and
Municode shall update and codify the following language as follows:
Sec. 4-61. – Releasing Animals In Public Places in the Corporate City Limits.
(c)

Exceptions.
(1) This Section does not apply to feral cats released as part of the City TNR
program.
(2) This section does not apply to cats released as part of the City of Cabot Community
Cat Program.
SECTION 4: Chapter 4, Animals, Article III. – Animal Care and Control § 4-65. –

Public Nuisance Animals is hereby amended and Municode shall update and codify the
following language as follows:
Sec. 4-65. – Public Nuisance Animals.
(10) Any Community Cat Colony within the corporate city limits of Cabot, which has not
had all cats sterilized or vaccinated.
SECTION 5: Chapter 4, Animals, Article III. – Animal Care and Control § 4-70. –
Impoundment and Destruction Authorized is hereby amended and Municode shall update and
codify the following language as follows:
Sec. 4-70 Impoundment and Destruction Authorized.
(b) Such impounded animal shall be held for a period of five (5) business
days, at the end of which time the animal becomes the property of the City
of Cabot and may be adopted, transferred, or humanely Euthanized in cases
of

aggression,

untreatable/manageable illness

or

injury, unmanageable behavior issues resulting in the animal being
unadoptable.
(c) Such animal may be humanely euthanized prior to the expiration of

such five (5) business day waiting period when such animal has been
seriously injured or seriously ill and humane euthanasia would eliminate
suffering on the part of the animal and would constitute the humane solution
to such animal's suffering.
(d) Such animal may be euthanized prior to the expiration of such five (5)
business day waiting period when such an animal presents itself in a vicious
or dangerous manner that places the public or Cabot Animal Services
Employees in ongoing danger and such euthanasia would eliminate this
threat.
(e) Such animal may be released as part of the City of Cabot Community
Cat Program.
SECTION 6: Chapter 4, Animals, Article IV. – Dogs and Cats § 4-103. – Running At
Large Prohibited is hereby amended and Municode shall update and codify the following
language as follows:
4-103. – Running At Large Prohibited.
(b) Exceptions.
(1) Feral cats that have been trapped, spayed or neutered and released are exempt
from this section. Each cat would be ear-tipped, clearly identifying it as a product of the city
TNR program.
(2) Community cats are exempt from this section as part of the City of Cabot
Community Cat Program. Each cat would be ear-tipped, clearly identifying it as a part of
the City of Cabot Community Cat Program.
SECTION 7: Chapter 4, Animals, Article V. – Feral Cat Colonies shall be repealed in
its entirety and replaced with the following regulations shall be codified using the same format as
the current code, as follows:
Section 1: Purpose of Section
(a) Community Cat Management Initiatives: The City of Cabot recognizes the
need for innovation in addressing the issues presented by feral, free-roaming and other
community cats. To that end it recognizes that there are community care givers of cats,

and acknowledges that properly managed community cats may be part of the solution to
the continuing euthanasia of cats; and establishes the following requirements:
(1) All community cats must be maintained on private property of the with
permission on the private property landowner (including city, state, and federal
public property).
(2) A community cat caregiver certification program may be developed to
educate people about community cats, the importance of a veterinary provider
relationship to best address community cat needs, common disease(s) & proper
care, good management practices, and maintenance of the community cats. The
educational program shall be developed by Cabot Animal Services.
(3) All cats that are part of the community cat management program must
be sterilized, vaccinated against the threat of rabies, and ear-tipped on the left ear
for easy identification; if these requirements are met the community cat is exempt
from stray and at-large provisions of this ordinance that apply to owned animals.
(4) If a person is providing care for the community cats, he or she is
required to provide certain necessities on a regular/ongoing basis, including, but
not limited to, proper nutrition and medical care as needed. If medical care is
unavailable or too expensive, the caregiver must not allow the cat to suffer.
(i) Food must be provided in the proper quantity for the number of
cats being managed and is to be supplied no less than once per day. Food
must be maintained in proper feeding containers.
(ii) Water must be clean, potable and free from debris and algae.
(iii) Shelter shall be unobtrusive, safe, and of the proper size for
the cat(s).
(5) Any cat received by Cabot Animal Services may be returned to the
location where picked up after neutering, eartipping, vaccination against rabies
unless further veterinary care is required, or a home is found for the cat (unless
found to be a Public Nuisance Animal).
(6) A trapped, eartipped cat, unless found to be a Public Nuisance Animal,
will be released on site unless further veterinary care is required, in which case
the cat will be returned once it no longer needs care.
(b) Working Cat Management Initiatives: The City of Cabot recognizes the need
for innovation in environmental protection from harmful pesticides and rodenticides. A
working cats program is designed to place cats in safe environments where they are
valued for their hunting skills as working cats. This program will be offered by the Cabot
Animal Shelter for use with otherwise unadoptable cats in the program as an alternative
to euthanasia. The cats may not be suitable for adoption because they are feral cats or did
not acclimate to living in close quarters with humans. The City of Cabot Working cats
program will provide cats that are spayed or neutered, fully vaccinated, eartipped to
individuals and businesses and in exchange for their services, the cats are to receive a
place to live, food, water, and vet care as described in this ordinance.

1) All Working cats must be maintained on private property of the with
permission on the private property landowner (including city, state, and federal
public property).
(2) A working cat caregiver certification program may be developed to
educate people about community cats, the importance of a veterinary provider
relationship to best address community cat needs, common disease(s) & proper
care, good management practices, and maintenance of the community cats. The
educational program shall be developed by Cabot Animal Services.
(3) All cats that are part of the working cat program must be sterilized,
vaccinated against the threat of rabies, and ear-tipped on the left ear for easy
identification; if these requirements are met the working cat is exempt from stray
and at-large provisions of this ordinance that apply to owned animals.
(4) If a person is providing care for the working cats, he or she is required
to provide certain necessities on a regular/ongoing basis, including, but not
limited to, proper nutrition and medical care as needed. If medical care is
unavailable or too expensive, the caregiver must not allow the cat to suffer.
(i) Food must be provided in the proper quantity for the number of
cats being managed and is to be supplied no less than once per day. Food
must be maintained in proper feeding containers.
(ii) Water must be clean, potable and free from debris and algae.
(iii) Shelter shall be unobtrusive, safe, and of the proper size for
the cat(s).
(5) A trapped, eartipped cat, unless found to be a Public Nuisance Animal,
will be released on site unless further veterinary care is required, in which case
the cat will be returned once it no longer needs care.
SECTION 8: Repealer. All Ordinances and parts of Ordinances, in conflict herewith
are hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict; specifically, parts and sections delineated herein
are hereby repealed.
