CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Council Meeting Minutes
April 20, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly
Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised.
This allowed for ten feet of spacing between chairs, as suggested. The meeting was
both open to the public and an online meeting with video through the web-based
video conferencing tool Zoom. The City experienced technical difficulties during
the meeting and was unable to broadcast through Facebook Live consistently.

Call to Order
Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City Council
at 7:00 p.m. on April 20, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event Center. The opening
prayer was given and the Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Kincade.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Ronald
Waymack and Doug Warner attended the meeting in person and via Zoom. Council
Members Damon Bivins, Norma Naquin, James Reid, Matt Webber, Kevin Davis
and Ed Long all attended the meeting via Zoom. Also in attendance were City
Attorney Ben Hooper (via Zoom), City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, IT
Director Roger Self and HR Director Matthew Hood. Several members of the
public were also in attendance.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

The minutes of the March 30, 2020 Council Meeting were approved with a motion
by Mr. Davis and second by Mr. Bivins. Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call
Vote.

Motion to read legislation by title only by Mr. Warner, second by Mr. Bivins.
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Council Meeting Minutes
April 20, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly
Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised.
This allowed for ten feet of spacing between chairs, as suggested. The meeting was
both open to the public and an online meeting with video through the web-based
video conferencing tool Zoom. The City experienced technical difficulties during
the meeting and was unable to broadcast through Facebook Live consistently.

Call to Order

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City Council
at 7:00 p.m. on April 20, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event Center. The opening
prayer was given and the Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Kincade.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Ronald
Waymack and Doug Warner attended the meeting in person and via Zoom. Council
Members Damon Bivins, Norma Naquin, James Reid, Matt Webber, Kevin Davis
and Ed Long all attended the meeting via Zoom. Also in attendance were City
Attorney Ben Hooper (via Zoom), City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, IT
Director Roger Self and HR Director Matthew Hood. Several members of the
public were also in attendance.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Parks Event Center
May 4, 2020
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing
by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Work Session
to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for ten
feet of spacing between chairs, as suggested. The meeting was both open to the public
and an online meeting with video through the web-based video conferencing tool Zoom.
The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.

Council members present via Zoom were: Ed Long, James Reid, Damon Bivins, Kevin
Davis, and Matt Webber. Doug Warner attended the meeting in person. Norma Naquin
and Ron Waymack were absent. Others present: Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben
Hooper (via Zoom), City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, and Roger Self, IT Director.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid & Webber)

As Chairman, Ed Long, opened with discussion on an amendment to the Animal
Services Code regarding chickens. Spencer Dunlap, founding Pastor of Renew Community
Church addressed the council in support of allowing chickens within the City Limits of
Cabot. He would like to train people in raising chickens as one way to help solve hunger.
There were three others in attendance in support of allowing chickens and voiced their
agreement with Pastor Dunlap’s remarks. Phil Robinson voiced his opposition to allowing
chickens inside the City Limits due to chicken related diseases and other concerns.
Discussion. Motion to send this legislation to full council in May by Long, second by Reid.
Motion passed by a vote of 3-0. One person, via YouTube acknowledged support of this
legislation.

Budget & Personnel Committee Business: (Members are: Warner, Webber &
Naquin)

As Chairman, Doug Warner, stated there was nothing on the agenda for tonight.
However, he would like to report on the revenue numbers next month. Mayor Kincade
and others voiced their hope that Cabot would be fine and not suffer great loss in sales
tax due to the COVID-19 Pandemic and subsequent business closings.

Police & Fire Committee Business: (Members are: Bivins, Waymack and Long)

As Chairman, Damon Bivins opened with discussion on the MEMS interlocal
agreement. Discussion. It was determined the City is no longer contractually obligated
to respond to medical calls and the contract no longer will have a subsidy clause in it.
James Reid asked that MEMS use our local hospital as much as possible. Motion to send
this legislation to full council in May by Damon, second by Ed. Motion passed with a vote
of 2-0. Chief Boswell asked the council to consider the expense of refurbishing a fire

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
engine that was purchased in 2005. Due to timing issues of the vendor the payment
would not have to be managed until July or August of 2021. Discussion.

Community Development Committee Business: (Members are: Davis, Bivins and
Naquin)

As Chairman, Kevin stated there was nothing on the agenda for tonight. He
reminded all that Amy Williams, President/CEO Cabot Chamber of Commerce has already
provided the first quarter report on economic development to the council via email.

Military Affairs Committee Business: (Members are: Waymack, Warner, Reid)
Chairman Ron Waymack was absent — no action

Mayor Kincade announced - Mitch Ward donated a 2018 fifteen passenger van to The
PEAK Center.

Phil Robinson thanked all for the continued work it took to successfully stream this council
meeting.

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Council Meeting Minutes
May 18, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The meeting was both open to the public and an online meeting
with video through the web-based video conferencing tool Zoom. The event
was successfully streamed through YouTube.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 7:01 p.m. on May 18, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event Center.
The opening prayer was given and the Pledge of Allegiance was led by
Mayor Kincade.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
Ronald Waymack and Doug Warner attended the meeting in person. Council
Members Damon Bivins, Norma Naquin, James Reid, Matt Webber, and Ed
Long all attended the meeting via Zoom. Kevin Davis was absent. Also in
attendance were City Attorney Ben Hooper (via Zoom), City Clerk &
Treasurer Tammy Yocom, and IT Director Roger Self. Several members of
the public were also in attendance.
